newsitem.title: USA: New Holland confident of meeting 1997 targets.
newsitem.headline: New Holland confident of meeting 1997 targets.

text.p: New Holland NV said on Thursday it is optimistic about the future and confident of meeting its ambitious targets for 1997.

Chief Executive Officer Umberto Quadrino said "With a solid outlook for the agricultural equipment market, and our growing presence in North America, Europe, and around the world, we are optimistic about the future and confident of meeting the ambitious targets we set for ourselves in 1997."
Tom Kennedy, chief marketing officer, said the favorable economic fundamentals seen in the first half of the year should remain in place through the balance of 1997.

The company said its net sales from equipment operations were $1.650 billion for the second quarter ended June 30, up 10 percent from $1.506 billion in 1996. Revenue growth was strongest in North America, up 36 percent over the second quarter last year, a period in which the company said a concerted effort to reduce dealer inventory, coupled with limited availability of its new products, depressed revenues.
"Commodity prices have held up reasonably well during the first half of the year, contributing to an overall stable market for equipment sales," said Kennedy.

Kennedy said, "In North America, we continue to expect tractor industry demand to remain somewhat above 1996 levels through the year. In Brazil and other Latin American countries, industry demand has increased substantially in 1997, and we expect this trend to continue through the year.
"Across the markets of Africa and the Middle East industry sales have been running ahead of last year, and we expect to see positive results in these markets," added Kennedy.
"Across Western Europe, (however,) we expect to see a modest decline in industry sales of agricultural tractors, particularly in France and the UK." said Kennedy.

Furthermore, Kennedy continued, "Tractor demand in the Asia/Pacific region has weakened in several markets, including Japan, and now with dry weather conditions in Australia, and the recent currency devaluation in Thailand, we expect the Asia Pacific market to be down for the year."
"Our outlook for the combine harvester industry remains positive," concluded Kennedy.
New Holland, a Netherlands corporation, is a major global maker of tractors and other agricultural equipment which was wholly owned by Fiat SpA prior to its November 1996 initial public offering.
